cards.front: Recall a key point about Digital Design Tools and Techniques
cards.back: Vector graphics (Illustrator) use mathematical paths — they scale infinitely without quality loss; ideal for logos and illustrations.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Digital Design Tools and Techniques
cards.back: Raster images (Photoshop) are pixel-based — they lose quality when enlarged; ideal for photo editing and digital painting.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Digital Design Tools and Techniques
cards.back: Resolution matters: 72ppi for screen, 300ppi for print; RGB colour mode for screen, CMYK for print.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Digital Design Tools and Techniques
cards.back: Layers, masks and non-destructive editing allow you to experiment without permanently altering your original image.

cards.front: What should you know about graphic communication exam tips?
cards.back: Show SCREENSHOTS of your working process. Include layers panel, tools used, settings. Explain WHY you chose each tool. Compare digital and hand-rendered versions of the same idea.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: Photoshop is the best tool for all graphic design — logos, posters, everything. Correct: Photoshop is for RASTER (pixel) work — photo editing, digital painting. Illustrator is for VECTOR work — logos, icons, illustrations that need to scale. InDesign is for LAYOUT — multi-page documents. Choose the right tool for the task.
Use both vector and raster software to develop a design project. Show how you combine tools and techniques, annotate your workflow, and explain why each tool was appropriate for each task.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Digital Design Tools and Techniques
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Digital Design Tools and Techniques using appropriate art vocabulary. Identify techniques, materials and processes accurately.
